gardens.title: Butterfly Garden
gardens.blurb: Nectar shrubs and perennials suited to Delaware Zone 7.
gardens.story: Built around summersweet, spicebush, butterfly bush, and colorful borders that feed pollinators from spring through fall.
gardens.bestFor: Front yards and sunny side beds
tips: Skip pesticides — caterpillars need the leaves.

gardens.title: Pollinator Patch
gardens.blurb: A sunny patch of roses, catmint, salvia, and native grasses.
gardens.story: Easy color for bees and butterflies with Knock Out roses, nepeta, and warm-season grasses.
tips: Leave grass seed heads for winter birds.

gardens.title: Privacy Screen
gardens.blurb: Arborvitae, hollies, and upright evergreens for year-round privacy.
gardens.story: A living fence of Emerald Green, Green Giant, and structured hollies that block neighbors without a fence permit.
tips: Water weekly the first two summers.
Mix heights for a natural look.

gardens.title: Shade Garden
gardens.blurb: Azaleas, hostas, hydrangeas, and ferns for dappled beds.
gardens.story: Layered shade planting with evergreen azaleas, oakleaf hydrangea, and hosta texture.
tips: Morning sun is fine for many hydrangeas.
Group hostas for a carpet effect.

gardens.title: Cottage Garden
gardens.blurb: Hydrangeas, roses, spirea, and lilacs in a relaxed border.
gardens.story: A welcoming front-yard border with repeating blooms and soft structure.
tips: Mix heights: tall back, low front.
Add one fragrant lilac or viburnum.

gardens.title: Delaware Natives
gardens.blurb: Spicebush, summersweet, chokeberry, little bluestem, and more.
gardens.story: Plants that belong here — better for birds, butterflies, and lower long-term care.
tips: Start with one native shrub and one grass.

gardens.title: Four-Season Structure
gardens.blurb: Evergreens, winter berries, spring bloom, and fall color.
gardens.story: A backbone of evergreens with winterberry, red maple, and seasonal flowering shrubs.
tips: Finish with fall color and berries.
